newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 3.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The 90-year-old Australian PGA Championship which was under threat of extinction due to the lack of a sponsor has been saved from golfing oblivion with the announcement of multi-million dollar deal with MasterCard International. The tournament will be played at the New South Wales Golf Club from November 14-17. Page 20.

Sydney proved it has kept its Australian Football League enthusiasm with a rousing public reception for the Sydney Swans in Martin Place yesterday. The grand final losers could have been mistaken for finals winners as a packed lunchtime crowd came out to tell the team they were still the city's favourite. Page 20.

Despite being the third Illawarra Steelers coach in just over a year, Andrew Farrar has welcomed the pressure of his new posting. Despite receiving only a one-season contract, the former rugby league international said he is focusing on his
team making th finals next season. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian soccer coach Eddie Thomson is expected to leave for Japan next week as part of negotiations with the Hiroshima club. It is understood Thomson has been offered a package worth around A$500,000 a season. Australian Soccer officials have resigned hemselves to losing Thomson who has been head coach for over five years. Page 44.

A fourth Australian provincial Rugby Union team based either in Perth or Melbourne is tipped to enter the Super 12 competition as early as next season. ARFU chief executive John O'Neill said that his union is strongly looking for the inclusion of a fourth Australian team for the competition. Page 44.
Matt Burke of the Waratahs and Wallabies was last night awarded The Sydney Morning Herald's Rugby Player of the Year award. Page 44.
THE AGE

Wayne Jackson yesterday became the most powerful man in the Australian Football League. As newly-appointed chief executive of the league, AFL clubs have overwhelmingly endorsed Jackson's appointment. However, the clubs have urged the former SANFL player to be compassionate in relation to mergers and other ills affecting Victorian-based clubs. Page B8.

Richmond's Tony Free, who faces more major surgery on his injured knee, has resigned as captain and will miss next season. The AFL star hopes to return to form in 1998 but for the meantime he has been kept on the Tigers' list and appointed development coach. Page B8.

North Melbourne Giants import Paul Maley has been ruled out of tomorrow's first National Basketball League quarter-final against South East Melbourne because of his back injury. Maley sustained the injury in last Friday's loss to Adelaide. Page B8. - - - -
HERALD SUN

Melbourne Tigers captain Andrew Gaze said the team's strong season will all be for nothing if they don't take out the National Basketball League championship. In Saturday night's clash against Brisbane, Gaze is concerned about complacency in the Tiger's rnks, but he anticipates a win in the play-off. Page 82.

Victorian-born Graeme Lloyd is the first Australian to play in the US baseball major league post-season play, appearing for the New York Yankees in the American league series opener against the Texas Rangers. Although the Yankees lost 6-2, the southpaw piched a perfect innings. Page 82.

New Australian Football League chief Wayne Jackson has identified the future of the AFL's Waverly Park as one of the 10 issues which will be taken on board by the commission. Jackson also noted other areas to be looked at include the number of Melbourne sdes, State-of-origin football and AFL in the northern
states. Page 88.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

After a Rugby Union Appeals Tribunal upheld a striking charge against Randwick flanker Michael Cheika last night, Cheika announced his retirement and called for changes to the judicial system. Page 85.

According to Rugby Football League chief executive Maurice Lindsay, if Super League wins its Federal Court appeal on Friday, Great Britain may play against Australia during the Lions' current South Pacific tour. Page 87.

Sky Channel, Australia's satellite racing broadcaster, continues the second day of blackouts on Victorian TAB agencies after negotiations between the broadcaster and Victoria's TABCorp broke down. The Victorian Racing Club has labelled Sky's 164 per cent fee increase as "extortion". Page 92.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
